# `budget` commands

## `budget clear`

Clear budget amounts: one account row (account), one customer or class (customer / class_id), both, or the whole budget when neither is named, as the anchor's Clear button does. Every cleared amount is audited with its value before, so nothing is lost from the trail.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | account |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/budget.clear` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow budget clear "Plan 2026" --account Rent --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Start rent over" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "budget clear", "input": {"budget": "Plan 2026", "account": "Rent"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer or job, by id or full name; required on a customer budget, refused on any other. |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Class, by id or full name; required on a class budget, refused on any other. |

## `budget create`

Create a budget: a named plan for one fiscal year with one amount per account per month, as the anchor's Set Up Budgets builds one. kind profit_and_loss budgets income and expense (each month's net); balance_sheet budgets each asset, liability and equity account's ending balance. A profit and loss budget can be kept per customer:job (by=customer) or per class (by=class). from_actuals fills it from the previous fiscal year's actual figures month by month, on the company report basis unless basis is given. Amounts are in the statement sign, so income and expense are both positive. Several budgets may cover the same year under different names. A budget never posts to the ledger.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | account |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/budget.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow budget create --name "Plan 2026" --fiscal-year 2026 --from-actuals --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Next year's budget" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "budget create", "input": {"name": "Plan 2026", "fiscal_year": 2026, "from_actuals": true}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `--name` | string | yes | no | — | Name for the budget; unique within the company, ignoring case.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `fiscal_year` | `--fiscal-year` | integer | yes | no | — | Fiscal year to budget, named by the calendar year it starts in. The budget has one column per month of that fiscal year.; minimum 1; maximum 9998 |
| `kind` | `--kind` | literal["profit_and_loss", "balance_sheet"] | no | no | "profit_and_loss" | profit_and_loss: income and expense per month. balance_sheet: the ending balance of each asset, liability and equity account per month. |
| `by` | `--by` | literal["none", "customer", "class"] | no | no | "none" | none for one company budget; customer or class to keep amounts per customer:job or per class (profit and loss only). |
| `from_actuals` | `--from-actuals` | boolean | no | no | false | Fill the budget from the previous fiscal year's actual figures, month by month (per customer:job or class when the budget is kept that way). Off: the budget starts empty. |
| `basis` | `--basis` | literal["accrual", "cash"] \| null | no | yes | null | Cash or accrual for this report only. Omit to use the company report basis. Cash reports use current matching evidence and can restate earlier periods after matching changes. |

## `budget delete`

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `budget fill`

Fill one account row from start_month through through_month (defaults: the whole year). The first month takes amount -- or, when amount is omitted, the amount already in start_month, which is the anchor's Copy Across. Each later month takes the month before plus change, or the month before changed by change_percent (compounding, rounded to the cent half to even: 5000.00 at 1 gives 5050.00, 5100.50, ...); with neither, every month takes the first amount. Audited like budget set.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | account |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/budget.fill` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow budget fill "Plan 2026" --account Rent --amount 1000.00 --change-percent 1 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Rent rises 1% a month" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "budget fill", "input": {"budget": "Plan 2026", "account": "Rent", "amount": "1000.00", "change_percent": "1"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer or job, by id or full name; required on a customer budget, refused on any other. |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Class, by id or full name; required on a class budget, refused on any other. |
| `budget` | `BUDGET` | string | yes | no | — | Budget id, or its exact name (ignoring case).; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `account` | `--account` | string | yes | no | — | Account whose row is filled, by id, full name or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `start_month` | `--start-month` | string \| null | no | yes | null | First month filled; omitted, the first month of the budget. |
| `through_month` | `--through-month` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Last month filled; omitted, the last month of the budget. |
| `amount` | `--amount` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Amount for start_month. Omitted, the amount already in start_month is copied across (the anchor's Copy Across). |
| `change` | `--change` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Added to each month after the first, compounding: 5000.00 with change 100.00 gives 5000.00, 5100.00, 5200.00, ... |
| `change_percent` | `--change-percent` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Percent each month changes from the month before, compounding and rounded to the cent half to even: 5000.00 at 1 gives 5000.00, 5050.00, 5100.50, ...; negative to decrease. |

## `budget set`

Set the amounts of one account row of a budget for consecutive months, from start_month (default the first month). 0 or an empty amount clears that month; months not given are left alone. On a customer or class budget, name the customer or class the row is for. The account must be active and of the budget's kind. Exact decimal amounts in the home currency; negative amounts are allowed. Every changed month is audited with its amount before and after, and the budget version goes up by one.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | account |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/budget.set` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow budget set "Plan 2026" --account "Service Income" --start-month 2026-03 --amounts '["1750.00","1800.00"]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Spring estimate" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "budget set", "input": {"budget": "Plan 2026", "account": "Service Income", "start_month": "2026-03", "amounts": ["1750.00", "1800.00"]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer or job, by id or full name; required on a customer budget, refused on any other. |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Class, by id or full name; required on a class budget, refused on any other. |
| `budget` | `BUDGET` | string | yes | no | — | Budget id, or its exact name (ignoring case).; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `account` | `--account` | string | yes | no | — | Account to budget, by id, full name or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `start_month` | `--start-month` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Month the first amount is for; omitted, the first month of the budget. |
| `amounts` | `--amounts` | array[string] | yes | no | — | Amounts for consecutive months from start_month, e.g. ['1000.00','1000.00','1250.00']. 0 or an empty string clears that month. Months not given are left alone. |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Version returned by budget show; a stale write is refused. |

## `budget show`

Show a budget as its entry grid: one row per account (and per customer or class on a customer or class budget) with an amount for each of the twelve months and the annual total, in statement then account order, with net income budgeted per month. Name customer or class_id to see one.

| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VALUE_RANGE` | The value is outside its allowed range or storage bounds. |
